headline: Bruins looking to rebound against Minnesota after that Montreal catastrophe
morning_brew: It has been a miserable couple of days in the Hub since that absolute gut punch against the Canadiens. Losing to Montreal is never something you just wash down with a medium regular from Dunks, especially when it snaps a home winning streak like that. I have spent the last forty-eight hours staring at the wall wondering what the hell went sideways on the ice, and the defensive effort was a total disastah. We let them dictate the pace for way too long, and you simply cannot hand points to a rival like that and hope to survive the week.

Saturday night offers us a chance to get things back on track when the Wild roll into the Garden. Minnesota is a tough, gritty team that plays a heavy style of hockey, so we are going to need a full sixty minutes from the opening drop of the puck. It is time for the boys to shove that last performance into the incinerator, tighten up the coverage in our own zone, and get back to the kind of shutdown hockey that makes our barn such a nightmare for visitors.

I am looking for a real bounce-back effort from the leadership group. We have the talent to run with anyone in the league, but talent doesn't mean a damn thing if you don't show up with the right mindset (and I swear, if Uncle Carmine falls asleep on the couch during the first period again, I am locking him in the guest room). I will be in my seat early, and if the boys play with the desperation this team is capable of, I am confident we can get back to our winning ways. It is a big night to regain our footing, and I am ready to see us remind everyone why this squad is a force to be reckoned with.

news_digest.dans_take: I watched that third period through my fingers like a horror movie, but we move.
